hints.title: Average Sessions Per Active User
hints.text: Determine the average number of unique sessions per active user over the thirty days ending 2019-07-27, defaulting to zero if empty.

hints.title: Distinct Counting with Null-Safe Ratio
hints.text: Count distinct session identifiers divided by distinct user identifiers within the date window, applying round and coalesce.

hints.title: Average Sessions Query Blueprint
hints.text: select ifnull(round(count(distinct session_id) / count(distinct user_id), 2), 0.00) as average_sessions_per_user from Activity where activity_date between "2019-06-28" and "2019-07-27".

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT IFNULL(ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), 2), 0.00) AS average_sessions_per_user
FROM Activity
WHERE activity_date BETWEEN '2019-06-28' AND '2019-07-27';
```

complexity.notes: Single scan with hash sets for distinct users and sessions executes in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Failing to handle empty tables causes division-by-zero or unexpected null values.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Global aggregation performs distinct counting without grouping by individual user.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of IFNULL / COALESCE to handle empty activity sets and division by zero.

solutions.approach: Single-Pass Distinct Session and User Ratio
PostgreSQL Null-Safe Distinct Ratio with Numeric Round

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def user_activity(activity: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    filtered = activity[(activity['activity_date'] >= '2019-06-28') & (activity['activity_date'] <= '2019-07-27')]
    users = filtered['user_id'].nunique()
    sessions = filtered['session_id'].nunique()
    avg = round(sessions / users, 2) if users > 0 else 0.0
    return pd.DataFrame({'average_sessions_per_user': [avg]})
